answers.answer: For two Spirits, the Fear Pool starts with 8 markers (4 per Spirit). Use 9 Fear Cards: three, Terror II divider, three, Terror III divider, three; start at Terror I. For the Invader deck, remove one card of each stage unseen, then stack 3 Stage I, 4 Stage II and 5 Stage III cards; place the 12-card deck in Explore. With a Blight Card, use 2 per Spirit plus 1 additional total (5 for two Spirits) on its Healthy side. Without a card, use the printed pool of 5 per Spirit plus 1 total (11 for two Spirits). Reveal and resolve the top Invader card as the initial Explore, then put it face-up in Build; that Explore completes setup and Ravage starts empty.
answers.evidence: Setup: “4 Fear markers per Spirit”; Fear Cards are “three cards, Terror II divider, three cards, Terror III divider, three cards.” Invader deck setup specifies “3 Stage I…4 Stage II…5 Stage III.” Blight setup says “2 Blight per Spirit plus exactly 1 additional Blight total”; intro alternative says “5 Blight per Spirit +1 total.” Initial Explore is last part of setup; put it “face-up in Build.”

answers.answer: Yes. Resolve multiple Add Presence placements sequentially, so the first newly placed Presence can be the range origin for the second. Take the leftmost remaining disk from either Presence track for each placement. Energy and Card Plays track numbers do not add together; use the highest uncovered number on the respective track.
answers.evidence: Growth: “With multiple placements, resolve them sequentially: a newly placed disk may be the origin for the next”; take “the leftmost remaining disk from either Presence track.” Energy says “highest uncovered number”; Play/pay uses “highest uncovered Card Plays number.”

answers.answer: An Add Presence instruction may reposition any of the Spirit’s Presence already on the island, even if track disks remain or are exhausted. Measure range and choose the destination using existing Presence, including the disk being repositioned, then take a disk from anywhere on the island. Destroyed Presence cannot be used unless explicitly permitted.
answers.evidence: Growth: “You may instead reposition any of your island Presence, even with track disks remaining”; “measure range and select the destination using existing Presence, including the disk about to be repositioned.” “Destroyed Presence cannot be used unless explicitly permitted.”

answers.answer: Pay for all played cards, Fast and Slow, during the Spirit Phase and gain their printed Elements immediately when played. Fast-phase Energy cannot pay those earlier costs. Unspent Energy carries over; unused Card Plays do not carry over or save for another turn.
answers.evidence: Play and pay: pay printed costs “now, including Slow cards” and “Gain every played card’s printed Elements immediately.” “Energy expected from a Fast Power cannot pay these earlier Spirit-phase costs.” “Unspent Energy carries over”; Card Plays “cannot be shared or saved for a later turn.”

answers.answer: No. A Fast Power must be used in Fast or foregone; it cannot be saved for Slow. A Power cannot interrupt another Power; finish one Power before starting another. Select a Slow Power’s target when using it in the Slow Power Phase, based on the current board.
answers.evidence: Fast Phase: “A Power cannot interrupt another Power”; “A Fast Power cannot be saved for Slow.” Slow Phase: choose targets “now, based on the current board.”

answers.answer: The Town and Explorer deal 3 total Damage: 3 to the land, adding one Blight, and simultaneously 3 to the Dahan. The Dahan damage kills one Dahan and leaves the other with 1 marked Damage. The surviving Dahan counterattacks for 2 Damage; the players may assign it to destroy the Town. Destroying the Town generates 1 Fear.
answers.evidence: Ravage example gives exactly this setup: “3 land Damage (one Blight), and simultaneously 3 Dahan Damage (one dead, one damaged). The survivor can destroy the Town for 1 Fear.”

answers.answer: If Defend reduces Invader Damage to zero, surviving Dahan still counterattack for 2 each. If the entire Ravage was skipped, Dahan do not counterattack. Spirit Presence never counterattacks.
answers.evidence: Ravage: “Surviving Dahan counterattack even when Invader Damage was reduced to zero by Defend, but not when the entire Ravage was skipped. Presence never counterattacks.”

answers.answer: A land with only Explorers builds a Town. Equal numbers of Towns and Cities build a Town; more Towns than Cities build a City. A matching land with no Invaders builds nothing. Existing Towns are not removed or upgraded.
answers.evidence: Build: “with at least one Invader”; “More Towns than Cities: add a City”; “Otherwise, including equal counts or only Explorers: add a Town.” “Do not remove or upgrade an existing Town.”

answers.answer: A matching land Explores if it contains a Town or City, or is adjacent to a Town, City, or Ocean. Add one Explorer per qualifying land even if it has multiple sources. Explorers are not Explore sources. If an Invader card must be drawn and the deck is empty, the Spirits lose.
answers.evidence: Explore: add “one Explorer” to each matching land containing a Town/City or adjacent to a Town, City, or Ocean; multiple sources “still yield just one Explorer”; “Explorers do not act as sources.” Defeat routes: lose if “you must draw an Invader card to Explore but none remains.”

answers.answer: After resolving Explore, discard the old Ravage card, slide Build to Ravage, and move the just-revealed Explore card to Build. A Stage III card with two terrains affects both terrains, whose lands may be interleaved. Ignore Stage II flag/Escalation icons when there is no Adversary.
answers.evidence: Advance cards: “Discard the old Ravage card; slide Build to Ravage and the just-revealed Explore card to Build.” Stage III two terrains affect both; “Ignore Stage II flag/Escalation icons without an Adversary.”

answers.answer: With two Spirits, the Fear Pool has 8 markers. Moving 3 Fear when 7 are already generated completes one card: return all 8 markers to the Pool, earn the top Fear Card face-down, then move the remaining 2 Fear markers from the Pool to Generated Fear. Exposing Terror II changes the Terror Level immediately; its victory condition applies at the next outcome check. An earned card is face-down until the Fear step; if earned during the Fear step it is appended to the resolving stack and resolved that same step.
answers.evidence: Fear procedure: “When all 4 per Spirit markers have moved, earn the top Fear Card face-down, return all markers to the pool and continue with any leftover Fear.” Earning a card exposes the divider and the new Terror Level applies immediately; victory applies at outcome check. Fear step resolves earned cards; cards earned during that step are appended and resolved “this same step.” Summary does not specify a blanket reveal time outside the Fear step, beyond stating earned cards are face-down.

answers.answer: When Fear generated during the Fear step earns another card, append it to the bottom of the resolving stack and resolve it in that same Fear step. Resolve each card using the Terror Level current when it is resolved; subsequent cards use the newly reached level. “Each player” choices do not require that player’s Presence or Power Range unless the card explicitly says so.
answers.evidence: Fear step: cards earned during it “append them to the bottom of the resolving stack and resolve them this same step”; “Subsequent cards use any newly reached Terror Level.” Fear effects: choices can affect anywhere allowed “without the player’s own Presence or Power Range.”

answers.answer: Adding Blight to an already-Blighted land destroys one Presence from each Spirit with Presence there, not every disk. The players choose one adjacent land for the one-Blight cascade. If that adjacent land was already Blighted, add one Blight there, destroy one Presence from each Spirit there, and cascade one Blight to one adjacent land of the players’ choice.
answers.evidence: Blight procedure: destroy “one Presence from each Spirit with Presence there, not every disk.” If it “already had any Blight,” also add one Blight to one adjacent land chosen by players. Cascades destroy one disk per Spirit and continue if revisiting an already-Blighted land.

answers.answer: Setup Blight comes from the box, not the active pool; after setup, added Blight comes from the active card/board pool. When a Healthy card’s pool empties, follow the card’s instructions, flip/refill as directed, and continue unfinished additions/cascades. Add the reverse side’s printed number per Spirit from the box, without the setup +1. Removing Blight never makes a Blighted card Healthy again.
answers.evidence: Setup: setup Blight “comes from the box, never the Blight pool.” Blight procedure says take later Blight from active pool; on empty, follow instructions, flip/refill and continue; add reverse side printed number per Spirit, “do not add the initial +1 again.” “A Blighted card never becomes Healthy again.”

answers.answer: Elements are checked, not spent, and the same Elements can satisfy multiple Powers and thresholds. An Innate cannot be used twice just because the Spirit has twice its Elements. All levels of a Power use the same target land or Spirit; they cannot target separate lands. An “Instead” level replaces the earlier effects rather than adding to them.
answers.evidence: Using Powers and Elements: “Elements are checked, never spent”; same Elements can “satisfy multiple Powers and thresholds.” “You cannot…use an innate twice just by having twice its Elements.” Multiple effects and all innate levels apply to “that same target”; “Instead replaces previous effects.”

answers.answer: Yes. If the target is legal, inability to perform one instruction does not prevent using the Power; resolve as much as possible. After starting, the player cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction, though “up to” permits zero. The player may forego the whole Power, but receives no Energy refund.
answers.evidence: Power rules: “Inability to perform one instruction does not prohibit playing or using a Power on an otherwise legal target.” “Cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction”; may forego whole Power, “but cannot” recover Energy (Fast phase says no refund).

answers.answer: Choose Minor or Major, draw 4 (reshuffling that deck’s discard if needed), keep 1 in hand and discard the other 3 to that shared deck discard. After gaining a Major, Forget one of the Spirit’s cards permanently: it may come from hand, personal discard, or play, including the Major just gained. A forgotten Minor/Major goes to its shared deck discard; a forgotten Unique goes under the Spirit panel. Forgetting a card in play immediately removes its Elements and unused activation; any effect already resolved persists.
answers.evidence: Gain Power Card: “draw 4…keep 1 in hand, and discard the rest to that deck’s shared discard.” Major: Forget from hand, personal discard, or play, including newly gained Major. Forgotten Minor/Major to shared discard; Unique under panel. From play, “immediately lose its Elements and any unused activation; an already resolved effect persists normally.”

answers.answer: Damage marks Invaders and destroys them when marked Damage reaches Health; each destroyed Town gives 1 Fear and City 2, while Explorers give none automatically. Damage from separate normal Powers can accumulate within a turn. Normal Spirit Damage does not hurt Dahan or land. Destroy returns a piece regardless of Health and generates normal Town/City destruction Fear; Remove returns it without destruction Fear. Replace removes a piece and adds another while retaining marked Damage; the replacement generates no Fear merely for being placed, but may be destroyed by retained Damage and then generate its normal Fear.
answers.evidence: Damage section: Damage normally means to Invaders; separate Powers’ Damage can accumulate; normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan/land. Destroy returns regardless of Health; Town +1 Fear, City +2. Remove returns without destruction Fear. Replace retains marked Damage; if it destroys the new piece, destruction Fear applies normally.

answers.answer: Increased Power Range does not increase Gather/Push distance. Multiple pieces may come from or go to different adjacent lands. Ordinary movement cannot send pieces off the island or into the Ocean. “Up to” may be zero.
answers.evidence: Gather/Push: multiple pieces may come/go from/to different adjacent lands; “Increased Power Range does not increase Gather/Push distance”; ordinary movement cannot send pieces “into the Ocean”; “up to” may be zero.

answers.answer: Victory: Terror I requires no Invaders of any type; Terror II requires no Towns or Cities; Terror III requires no Cities; at Victory (after earning the last Fear Card), win regardless of Invaders and do not wait to resolve that card. Defeat occurs if any Spirit has no Presence left on the island, if the active Blight supply empties and its instructions say to lose, or if an Explore requires drawing a card but none remains. In a single Ravage, complete that land’s action tree, including cascades and Dahan counterattack, then check outcomes. If final required Invaders are removed at that point and the Spirit simultaneously loses its last Presence, the Spirits win a sacrifice victory. Do not finish other Ravage lands first.
answers.evidence: Scoring table states all four Terror victory conditions; Defeat routes lists the three loss routes. Outcome timing: finish “the current action and all actions it triggers,” check before “next land’s Invader action”; if both win and loss are met, “Spirits win a sacrifice victory.”
